newsitem.title: USA: Micron bounces back some after drubbing.
newsitem.headline: Micron bounces back some after drubbing.

text.p: Shares of Micron Technology rose in heavy trading on Thursday a day after the stock took a pounding after a key analyst downgraded the stock.
Shares rose 2-1/4 to 44-7/8 and were one of the most heavily traded issues on the New York Stock Exchange, with nearly 10 million shares traded.
Robertson Stephens & Co analyst Dan Niles made bullish comments on the stock, raising his price target over the next six months for Micron to $60 from a range of $50 to $55.

That recouped some of Wednesday's losses, when the stock closed down 7-1/2 to 42-5/8. The fall was sparked after formerly bullish Merrill Lynch analyst Tom Kurlak downgraded the stock and cut profit estimates, citing falling chip prices and problems with a 64 Meg transition.
Niles said in his research report that the estimates cut by Merrill Lynch may have been too high in the first place, since they were well above First Call consensus estimates.
He also said the 64 Meg transition, also cited by Merrill Lynch, is not likely to be a problem for Micron and noted that the company seems to be cutting costs well.
